Yom Kippur Lox and Bagel Platter

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Serves 6-8Prep 20 min

After the solemnity and fasting of Yom Kippur, breaking the fast is a moment of communal comfort and gentle nourishment. A lox and bagel platter is a beloved tradition, offering a refreshing and satisfying spread that is easy to prepare and perfect for sharing with family and friends as the day of atonement concludes.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450 g) thinly sliced lox (smoked salmon)
  • 6-8 assorted bagels, sliced in half
  • 2 (8-ounce / 226 g) containers plain cream cheese, softened
  • 1 medium red onion, very thinly sliced
  • 2-3 ripe tomatoes, thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) capers, drained
  • 1/4 cup (about 4 g) fresh dill, roughly chopped
  • 2 lemons, cut into wedges

Method

  1. Arrange the thinly sliced lox artfully on a large serving platter, fanning out the slices or creating small rosettes.
  2. Place the softened cream cheese into small serving bowls. You can offer plain cream cheese in one bowl and mix some chopped chives or scallions into another for variety.
  3. Arrange the sliced bagels in a basket or on a separate platter alongside the lox.
  4. On the main platter or in separate small bowls, arrange the thinly sliced red onion, sliced tomatoes, and drained capers.
  5. Garnish the lox platter generously with the fresh dill.
  6. Place lemon wedges around the platter for guests to squeeze over their lox.
  7. Serve immediately, allowing guests to assemble their own bagels with their preferred toppings.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, offer a variety of cream cheeses, such as scallion, vegetable, or even a dill-infused cream cheese.
  • Add other fresh vegetables like thinly sliced cucumbers or radishes for additional crunch and color.
  • Ensure the cream cheese is at room temperature for easy spreading, and consider toasting the bagels just before serving for those who prefer them warm.
